AGENDA
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  JANUARY 24, 2024

  SPECIAL MEETING

  6:00 PM

  Rosa Barragan, Chair

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future
Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services
are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the Community Development Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during
regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5744.
You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  DECEMBER 13, 2023

Chair Barragan called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City
Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the provisions of
Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call in person were Commissioner Apodaca,
Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas and Chair Barragan. Vice Chair Lopez was
absent. Also present, via Zoom, were John P. Ramirez, Director of Community
Development; and, in person, Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; Jill Ann Arabe,
Development Services Manager; Manraj Bhatia, Senior Planner; Carlos Rojas, Associate
Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

REORGANIZATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION

After a short discussion on not having a full Commission present this evening, it was
moved by Chair Barragan and seconded by Commissioner Apodaca to table the
reorganization until such time that a full Commission is present.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE:
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas,
  and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Vice Chair Lopez

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of November
8, 2023.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2044
CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1031
CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1032
 Mort Goodarzi, MG Architects (“Applicant”); a request to permit a community
center/banquet facility within the existing 4,484 square feet building at 12156 Front
Street, and a religious assembly within the existing two-story, 1,996 square feet building
and parking lot redesign for shared use at 12169 Front Street. The subject properties
are 12156 and 12169 Front Street, located on the north and south sides of Front Street,
between Clarkdale Avenue and Funston Avenue, in the Commercial-Manufacturing (C-
M) zone. The project includes a request for:
(1) Precise Development Plan No. 2044: To reconfigure the parking lot for shared use;
(2) Conditional Use Permit No. 1031: To permit the community center/banquet hall use;
(3) Conditional Use Permit No. 1032: To permit the religious assembly use; and
(4) Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  Section 15303 (New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures).
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 13, 2023

Chair Barragan opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Bhatia
presented a report stating that the project involves two sites, 12156 Front Street and
12169 Front Street; that the property at 12156 Front Street is a request to permit a
community center/banquet hall facility within an existing 4,484 square foot building; that
the property at 12169 Front Street is to permit a religious assembly within an existing
two-story, 1,996 square foot building; and that the Precise Development Plan is a
request to redesign the existing parking lot at 12169 Front Street for shared parking
between the community center/banquet facility and religious assembly.

Further, she commented on the parking requirements indicating that for the banquet
hall at 12156 Front Street, 25 parking spaces are required; that 24 of those spaces will
be designated for shared parking at 12169 Front Street, which is across the street, and
that one handicap space is provided on site; that, in addition, ample street parking is
available; and that the hours of operation for the two uses will not overlap.

Ms. Bhatia shared that the project complies with the Zoning Code and General Plan as
well as being consistent with the Vision Plan for Front Street; that it is exempt from the
California Environmental Quality Act, and that it is staff’s recommendation that the
Commission adopt Resolutions Nos. 23-35, 23-36, and 23-37 to approve the project
subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibits “A”, and consider and find
that the project is exempt from CEQA under Section 15303 (New Construction or
Conversion of Small Structures).

In response to Commissioner Navas’ question how can they be sure that the hours of
operation are not going to overlap between the banquet hall and the church, Senior
Planner Bhatia indicated that the project has been conditioned to operate within the
hours indicated by the applicant, and that staff will ensure that the hours of operation
are adhered to.

Development Services Manager Arabe added that should any issues arise either with
the hours of operation or parking, staff would address those issues.

Commissioner Navas indicated that Front Street is an area that has been identified for
future development; that he also knows that a lot of people attend churches and stay
for prolonged periods of time; that the same applies to banquet halls; and that he has a
concern with parking overflowing into the street.

Commissioner Apodaca shared that they expect future uses for that location to be a
gathering place for restaurants, entertainment, etc.; that it is going to be hard to decipher
which establishment the people are going to; that, right now, it is almost a blank slate
that they are working with in anticipation of having people congregate in that area.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 13, 2023

Commissioner Garcia stated that, as part of the environmental review, the hours of
operation should be included. Development Services Manager Arabe indicated that
there is no environmental document associated with the project as they are proposing
to exempt it; however, there are conditions in place for each property; that, in addition,
there is a condition for a shared parking agreement to show what is required; that the
language within that agreement would specify that if there are any issues, for instance,
that resulted in overconcentration of parking within the street that were utilized by these
uses, those need to be controlled and addressed by the applicant; and that she believes
that they have sufficient documentation, as requested by the Commission, in the
conditions to ensure that potential future problems are going to be controlled.

Commissioner Navas stated that all of the Commissioners want Norwalk to thrive and
that they want to see Front Street as a place where people go to dine and shop and be
on their way; that his concern with the project is that should the applicant hold special
events at night; that he also does not want the City to be in a position where they are
sending Public Safety out as they are tying up parking for the restaurants and shopping.

Chair Barragan stated that all of the Commissioners’ comments are within the realm of
possibilities; and that she believes that they have conditions in place that will guide them
to address any issues that may come up.

Commissioner Garcia stated that their concern is that if they have two venues going on
at the same time with potential parking issues, this could be problematic.

Mr. Mort Goodarzi stated that he is the architect of the project. He indicated that they
have discussed the parking issues with the Planning Department; that, however, they
are open to any suggestions that might satisfy the Commission’s concern about
enforcing the limitations for the hours of use for each building.

In response to Commissioner Apodaca’s question how large is their congregation, Mr.
Goodarzi shared that when he went to a service there were approximately twelve people
in attendance; and he indicated that only a small group of people attend that
congregation.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed
the public hearing.

Commissioner Apodaca commented on the hours of operation for the church; that the
staff report identified the hours as follows: Mondays from 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.,
Thursdays from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.; and Saturdays from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.,
and she asked if it is correct that there is no service on Sundays. Ms. Bhatia indicated
that this is correct.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 4
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 13, 2023

In response to Commissioner Apodaca’s question on the ownership of the church and
the parking lot, Senior Planner Bhatia indicated that both the church and the banquet
hall facility are owned by the same ownership, but that the parking lot will be on the
church property.

Development Services Manager Arabe added that, with regards to the overall area of
Front Street and this area being a component of the Heart of Norwalk, they do intend
on creating a parking district for this area and looking at opportunities for additional
parking in addition to what is already provided on the street.

Commissioner Navas asked if, in the future, they decide that they no longer want a
church or a banquet hall, would the shared parking be grandfathered in? Senior Planner
Bhatia replied that this would depend on the proposed use.

Development Services Manager Arabe indicated that if the Commission so chooses,
they can condition it so that if a new use comes in to not have shared parking.

Commissioner Navas shared that this is a wonderful idea.

It was moved by Commissioner Garcia and seconded by Commissioner Apodaca, to:
(1) Adopt Resolution No. 23-35 to approve Conditional Use Permit No. 1031 subject to
  the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”, with an added condition that any
  future change of use or modification to the shared parking agreement shall require
  review and approval by the Planning Commission; and
(2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-36 to approve Conditional Use Permit No. 1032 subject to
  the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”, with an added condition that any
  future change of use or modification to the shared parking agreement shall require
  review and approval by the Planning Commission; and
(3) Adopt Resolution No. 23-37 to approve Precise Development Plan No. 2044 subject
  to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
(4) Considered and found that the project is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15303 (New Construction or
  Conversion of Small Structures).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE:
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas,
  and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Vice Chair Lopez

DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2023-14
Terry Womack, Go2Permitting, LLC, on behalf of California Fish Grill (“Applicant”); a
request to permit the on-site sale and consumption of alcohol (beer and wine) within a
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 5
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 13, 2023

2,357 square foot restaurant and 560 square foot outdoor dining area. The subject
property is generally known as 12539 Imperial Highway, Suite 101, located on the
northwest corner of Imperial Highway and Bloomfield Avenue (also known as
Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8025-025-006), in the Professional & Office (PO)
zone. The project includes a request for:
(1) Director Approval Request No. 2023-14: To permit the on-site sale and consumption
  of alcohol (beer and wine); and
(2) Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from CEQA pursuant
  to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities), licensing, operation, or minor alterations to an
  existing facility.

Chair Barragan opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Associate Planner Rojas
presented a report stating that the request is to permit the on-site sale and consumption
of beer and wine within a new 2,357 square foot California Fish Grill restaurant, with a
560 square foot outdoor dining area; that the subject site is located in the Norwalk
Fitness Village shopping center at the northwest corner of Imperial Highway and
Bloomfield Avenue in the Professional and Office (P/O) zone and has a General Plan
designation of Professional Office; that California Fish Grill is an upcoming restaurant
in the City; that the applicant is proposing the following hours of operation: Monday
through Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and Sundays from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00
p.m.; that the sale of alcohol is proposed to begin at 11:00 a.m. and end 30 minutes
before closing time; that tenant improvement plans include an interior remodel of the
restaurant and exterior remodel to the existing patio; that according to the applicant, the
restaurant is scheduled to open in June 2024; and that staff is recommending approval
of the project subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”.

Mr. Terry Womack, Go2Permitting, LLC stated that he is representing California Fish
Grill. He shared that they are very excited to come into Norwalk; that California Fish
Grill has at least forty-seven restaurants in California, three in Arizona and two in
Nevada; that they are continually growing since 1998; and that the alcohol sales are
approximately two to three percent of their sales. Further, he thanked Carlos Rojas for
presenting their report and the Commission for their consideration of the project.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed
the public hearing.

All of the Commissioners indicated that they are excited to see the California Fish Grill
restaurant coming into Norwalk and that they wished them much success.

It was moved by Commissioner Navas and seconded by Commissioner Apodaca to (1)
adopt Resolution No. 23-38 to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2023-14
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 6
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 13, 2023

subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (2) Considered and
found that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities), licensing, operation, or minor
alterations to an existing facility.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE:
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas,
  and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Vice Chair Lopez

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Development Services Manager Arabe shared that the applicant for the Quick Quack Car
Wash has appealed the Planning Commission’s denial of their request, and that the item
is going to City Council in January. Further, she commented on upcoming projects,
indicating that there has been a submittal for a large industrial building off of Carmenita
Road that is being scheduled for Planning Commission consideration.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 6:42 p.m.

  __________________________________
  ROSA BARRAGAN, CHAIR
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION

JOHN P. RAMIREZ, AICP, SECRETARY
NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
   Planning Commission
  Agenda Report
  January 24, 2024

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  John P. Ramirez, AICP, Director of Community Development

BY:  Andrew Arellano, Assistant Planner

SUBJECT: Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04 to permit the off-site sale and consumption of
  beer, wine, and distilled spirits (Type 21) within an existing 1,400 square feet
  convenience store on a 0.6-acre site. Environmental: Consider and find that the
  proposed project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).
  The subject property is 10710 Alondra Boulevard, located on the southeast corner of
  Alondra Boulevard and Piuma Avenue.

RECOMMENDATION

That the Planning Commission:

1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-01, to approve Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2023-04 subject
  to Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and

2. Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) Guidelines pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).

AUTHORITY
Section 17.02.210.A of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Planning
Commission of the City of Norwalk (“Planning Commission”) to grant a Conditional Use Permit
(“CUP”) for those uses which are so allowed by the Zoning Ordinance and impose certain
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04  January 24, 2024

conditions as it deems necessary and reasonable to protect the best interests of the
surrounding property or neighborhood and to ensure compliance with the general purpose and
intent of the Zoning Ordinance and the Norwalk General Plan.

Section 17.04.140 (Alcoholic beverage establishment) of the NMC requires that a CUP be filed
for alcoholic beverage establishments.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The 0.6-acre project site has a General Plan designation of Light Industrial and zoning of Light
Manufacturing (M-1). The project site is located on the southeast corner of Alondra Boulevard
and Piuma Avenue (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 7016-001-037).
Surrounding the project site is the San Gabriel River Freeway (Interstate 605) to the east and
north (across Alondra Boulevard), warehouse to the south, and drive-through (Del Taco)
restaurant to the west (across Piuma Avenue). The site currently contains an existing Shell
service station and convenience store.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant, Steve Rawlings on behalf of Jackson’s Food Store, is requesting to permit the
off-site sale of alcohol (Type 21- off-sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits) within an existing
1,400 square feet (Jacksons Food Market) convenience store. The convenience store currently
operates with a Type 20 (beer and wine) ABC license within the existing single store building.

The hours of operation are from 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily with 2-4 employees. At this time,
the applicant is not proposing any exterior or interior remodels to the existing building.

ANALYSIS

Subject Site Conditions Relating to Alcohol Sales

The following information is for Planning Commission consideration: 1) concentration of off-
site alcohol sales establishments, 2) neighborhood crime statistics, and 3) other alcohol
establishments within a quarter mile radius:
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04  January 24, 2024

  1. Concentration of off-site alcohol sales establishments – The request is to establish
  alcohol (beer, wine, and distilled spirits) sales for off-site consumption within an existing
  convenience store located in Census Tract No. 5530.

  The Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) has two types of off-site sales
  licenses, Type 20 & Type 21. Type 21 licenses are for off-sale beer, wine, and distilled
  spirits, which allows the sales of beer and wine for consumption off the premises where
  sold. This license allows for minors on the premises.

  According to ABC, there is currently one (1) off-sale alcohol establishment within
  Census Tract 5530. ABC recommends no more than three off-sale licenses within this
  census tract and therefore, the area is below the maximum concentration.

  The following is a table listing of all off-site alcohol sales establishments within Census
  Tract No. 5530:

  Existing Off-Sale Alcohol Establishments Within Census Tract No. 5530
  No. Business Name  Address  License Type

  1  7 Eleven  10656 Rosecrans Ave, Norwalk  21

  2. Neighborhood crime statistics – The subject site is located within the Los Angeles
  County Sheriff’s Department Reporting District No. 0455. According to a report issued
  by ABC, the number of Part 1 crime incidents (Part 1 crimes are defined by the Federal
  Government as criminal homicide, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny,
  theft, grand theft auto, and arson) in Reporting District No. 0455 in the last year was
  478. The City of Norwalk’s district average is 234.6 and a high crime district is any area
  with 20% above average Part I crime rate. The reporting district in which the Jackson’s
  Food Market proposes the sale of alcohol for off-site consumption is considered a high-
  crime reporting district.

  3.  Alcohol establishments within a quarter mile radius – The subject site is located at the
  southeast corner of Alondra Boulevard and Piuma Avenue. Within a quarter mile radius
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 4
Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04  January 24, 2024

  of the subject site, there is one (1) establishment with an on-site alcohol license and
  three (3) establishments with off-site alcohol licenses.

  Jacksons Food Stores, Inc. is a convenience store company that is rejuvenating the
  Norwalk Shell Service Station. The alcohol sales for off-site consumption is ancillary to
  the convenience store and will occur during business hours. It is not anticipated to
  generate detrimental impacts to the surrounding neighborhood.

  Due to the convenience store’s location within a high crime area, ABC requires a
  determination of Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN). The request must
  demonstrate an added benefit of convenience or necessity to the community. As
  discussed, the alcohol sales is ancillary to the existing 1,400 square feet convenience
  store, which will provide a variety of packaged foods and drinks. It will be a convenient
  service for patrons and the amount of sales is minimal in comparison to the overall
  goods and services provided. Furthermore, the closest alcoholic beverage
  establishment is a liquor store located 1,200 feet or 0.23 miles from the subject site. It
  does not provide the same services as the Jackson’s food market and service station.
  The convenience store with the off-sale license will serve the neighborhood and the
  surrounding community.

  In consideration of the current activity related to the site and proximity of surrounding
  sensitive uses, staff recommends approval with conditions that address the following
  issues:

  •  Limitations on quantities and size of alcoholic beverage containers
  •  Securing of alcohol
  •  Access to surveillance system and lighting for the site
  •  Training and education of employees regarding alcohol sales

  The alcohol sales for off-site consumption is consistent with the General Plan’s policies
  related to the Commercial Land Use category. The project encourages economic
  growth of a local business and enhancement of a service station and convenience
  store, which is important for the creation of a positive image for the City.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 5
Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04  January 24, 2024

Conditional Use Permit

The site is currently developed with an active Shell service station with 1,400 square feet
convenience store. Although no physical changes are proposed with this CUP request, the
existing site complies with all applicable code requirements. The convenience store currently
includes a sales floor, walk-in cooler, two restrooms, cashier area, and two entrances (one
main entry for the public and one employee entrance). Furthermore, the project will be
conditioned to comply with appropriate measures to monitor and ensure that the use will not
be detrimental to the community.

Parking and Site Circulation

Per the NMC, the parking requirement for the use is one space per 250 square feet of building
area, which results in six (6) stalls required. The site provides eight (8) parking spaces including
one (1) handicap accessible space.

Public Notification

Public hearing notices were published in The Norwalk Patriot on January 12, 2023, and posted
at locations set forth in NMC Section 1.08.030 as well as mailed to 28 property owners within
500 feet of the property. As of the writing of this report, staff has not received any
correspondence regarding the proposed project.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project will not have a
significant effect on the environment per Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA
Guidelines. Section 15301 exemption consists of operation, repair, maintenance, permitting,
licensing or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features involving negligible or no expansion of use. The proposed
project involves the off-site sale and consumption of alcohol within an existing convenience
store and service station.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 6
Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04  January 24, 2024

SUMMARY

The proposed project complies with all applicable regulations and, as conditioned, will not be
detrimental to the public health, safety and welfare of surrounding uses due to the ancillary
use to the service station. The alcohol sales is minimal compared to the sales and services
provided by the service station and convenience store and will not negatively impact the
community. The project is consistent with the General Plan vision of providing adequate local
serving commercial uses. Staff recommends approval of the proposed project subject to
conditions of approval.

ATTACHMENTS

A. Resolution No. 24-01 (Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-04)
B. Location and Vicinity Map
C. Site Plan and Floor Plan dated November 21, 2023
D. Code Requirements Letter
   ATTACHMENT A

  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-01

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA, SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND
  DECISION RELATIVE TO THE APPROVAL OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT
  NO. 2023-04

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk (“Planning Commission”)
has received Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2023-04, a request from Steve Rawlings
(“Applicant”), on behalf of Jacksons Food Stores Inc., for 10710 Alondra Boulevard, a request to
allow for off-site sale and consumption of beer, wine, and distilled spirits (Type 21 license) within
the existing 1,400 square feet convenience store (the “Project”); and

  WHEREAS, Section of 17.04.140 (Alcoholic beverage establishments) the Norwalk
Municipal Code (NMC) requires the review and approval of a CUP by the Planning Commission
for alcoholic beverage establishments; and

  WHEREAS, the purpose and intent of requiring a CUP is to ensure that compatibility is
maintained between a conditional use on a specific site and other existing and future land uses
on the adjacent and surrounding properties; and

  WHEREAS, Section 17.02.210 (Conditional use permits) of the NMC authorizes the
Planning Commission to grant a CUP and impose such conditions as it deems necessary and
reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property or neighborhood and to
ensure compliance with the Zoning Ordinance and the General Plan; and

  WHEREAS, the Project will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section
15301 (Existing Facilities) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), which consists of
operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, licensing or minor alteration of existing public or
private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible
or no expansion of use beyond that existing at the time; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing on
January 24, 2024 to consider CUP No. 2023-04, at which time oral and documentary evidence
related to the application were received.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The Planning Commission hereby finds and determines that the degree of
compatibility required by the Zoning Ordinance will be maintained with respect to the use of the
site, giving consideration to other existing and potential uses within the general area. The sale
and consumption of beer, wine, and distilled spirits off the market’s premises is not anticipated to
significantly impact surrounding uses in the area with the incorporation of conditions of approval.
Alcohol service and consumption will occur offsite only. The establishment is located within a
census tract that is not over concentrated with off-sale alcohol licenses. The business will adhere
to the Department of Public Safety’s Business Watch program and complete Responsible
Beverage Server training.

  Section 2. The subject property is located in the Light Manufacturing (M-1) zone and the
proposed sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits for off-site consumption is an added service for
 the market. The proposed use will comply with the zoning code and be consistent with General
Plan objectives and policies for providing adequate local-serving commercial uses, services
supporting economic growth, and establishing a positive image for Norwalk.

  Section 3. The proposed use will not be detrimental to the public health, safety, and
welfare of the community as it will be ancillary to the permitted convenience store. Alcohol
consumption will occur offsite only.

  Section 4. The sale and consumption of beer, wine and distilled spirits will generate
economic growth and revenue for the business. The convenience store with ancillary alcohol
sales will serve the neighborhood and surrounding community.

  Section 5. Public convenience and necessity will be served by the request to allow off-
sale of alcohol at the subject property because the proposed use is ancillary to a gas station,
which will provide a variety of packaged food and drinks. It is a convenient service for patrons as
they are purchasing gas and other goods. The closest alcoholic beverage establishment is a liquor
store located more than 1,200 feet from the subject site and does not provide the same services
as the Jackson’s Food Market. The convenience store with the off-sale license will serve the
neighborhood and surrounding community and will meet demand not met by the other existing
establishments.

  Section 6. The Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk, State of California, hereby
approves CUP No. 2023-04 subject to the conditions contained in attached Exhibit “A”.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: To permit the off-site sale and consumption of beer wine, and
distilled spirits (Type 21) within an existing 1,400 square feet market on a .60-acre site.

The following is a list of code requirements deemed applicable to the proposed project based
on plans stated above. The list is intended to assist the applicant by identifying requirements,
which must be satisfied during the various stages of project permitting and implementation.
A list of conditions of approval adopted by the Planning Commission in conjunction with the
requested entitlement(s), if any, will also be provided upon final project approval. If you have
any questions regarding these requirements, please contact the Plan Reviewer.

  1. Development Standards and Operations (NMC 17.04.140.I1)

  a. That off-sale alcoholic beverage establishments shall not sell or store motor
  fuels on the same premises as alcoholic beverages, except upon condition of
  the following:

  i. No beer or wine shall be displayed within five feet of the cash register
  or the front door unless it is in a permanently affixed cooler as of
  January 1, 1989.

  ii. No advertisements of alcoholic beverages shall be displayed at motor
  fuel islands.

  iii. No sale of alcoholic beverages shall be made from a drive-up window.

  iv. No display or sale of beer or wine shall be made from an ice tub.

  v. No beer or wine advertising shall be located on motor fuel islands and
  no self-illuminated advertising for beer or wine shall be located on
  buildings or windows.
 b. The noise level generated by the operation of such establishments shall not
  exceed forty-five (45) dBA on adjoining property zones or used for residential
  purposes.

c. Exterior lighting of the parking area shall be kept at an intensity of between
  one and two foot candles, so as to provide adequate lighting for patrons while
  not disturbing surrounding residential or commercial areas. Light sources shall
  be shielded.

d. The sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on premises shall be
  prohibited and appropriate posting of signs both inside and outside the
  establishment that drinking on the premises is prohibited by law.

e. Exterior storage of any kind shall be prohibited.

f. Litter and trash receptacles shall be located at convenient locations inside and
  outside the establishment, and operator of such establishment shall remove
  trash and debris on a daily basis.

g. Paper or plastic cups shall not be sold in quantities less than their usual and
  customary packaging.

h. That parking shall be provided in conformance with the off-street parking
  standards set forth in Chapter 17.03, Article II of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

i.  That no signs shall be installed on the site until a sign permit has been
  approved by the Planning and Building Divisions in conformance with the sign
  provisions set forth in Chapter 17.03, Article III of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

j.  The operator of the use shall provide night lighting and other security
  measures to the satisfaction of the Norwalk Sheriff’s Station.

k. The operator shall maintain the lot free and clear of trash and debris, and
  graffiti at all times.

l.  The operator of the use shall prevent loitering or other activity in the parking
  lot that would be a nuisance to adjacent uses and/or residential
  neighborhoods.
